title: Xenobots perform kinematic self-replication not known in any other species

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Xenobots perform kinematic self-replication not known in any other species

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Xenobots, proto-organisms that form spontaneously from dissociated frog embryo skin cells, are motile via cilia and perform kinematic self-replication, building copies of themselves from loose cells in the medium, a novel solution reached within 48 h without any evolutionary history of selection as Xenobots.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind › Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The most remarkable novel behavior is that of kinematic self-replication: Xenobots build copies of themselves by rearranging loose cells provided to them in the medium. This is Von Neumann-style replication that is not, to our knowledge, used by any other species on Earth.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Bioelectric networks: the cognitive glue enabling evolutionary scaling from physiology to mind”, Animal cognition (2023), doi:10.1007/s10071-023-01780-3; section “Basal cognition without neurons: what dynamic bodies think about › Creative problem-solving by adaptive morphogenesis: plasticity, not just emergent complexity”. Scope: Xenobots made from Xenopus laevis embryonic ectoderm (Kriegman et al. 2021a)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-glue-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.66

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The construction of offspring can be evaluated from public experimental media and published counts. The novelty claim and assertion about absence of selection history cannot be exhaustively resolved by the same dataset.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From public videos and counts, quantify whether parent Xenobots aggregate loose cells into viable motile offspring within 48 hours, while separately reviewing known reproductive modes for an equivalent process.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Selected videos may not represent all trials.

Demonstrating absence from every other species is an open-ended literature claim.

fields.value:
data existence: 0.7
discriminating power: 0.6

operationalizability: 0.78
analysis feasibility: 0.76

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The replication paper puts its counts and movies in the open supplement and releases the simulation code, so the reported Xenopus time course can be re-measured and the model re-run. That does not deposit raw offspring coordinates, and it does not contain a comparative survey of other species. The biological phenotype is therefore only partly checkable, and the simulation does not adjudicate the wet-lab result.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From the published movies and counts, score whether motile Xenopus ectoderm spheroids gather loose cells into piles that compact into further motile spheroids, and record the time from assembly to the first offspring. Offspring that swim and themselves pile cells would support kinematic replication on the reported timescale; piles that never become autonomous movers, or a requirement for a long selection history, would weaken it. A survey of other species is a separate test and is not in this archive.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No public survey tests the claim that no other species uses this mode.

The public code re-runs the design simulation; it does not replace the Petri-dish counts.

Pile formation can be passive flow-driven aggregation rather than construction of a copy.
